text: Chapter 3's Lesson 11 taught a four-part structure for documenting any project and said plainly that you were about to build a capstone of your own to apply it to, starting in Chapter 4. That capstone is now finished -- requirements gathered, built, tested, documented, presented, defended, and revised against a real peer-review finding. This lesson closes that loop, filling in all four components with this exact project.

The business problem, stated plainly, not as a feature list: three hospital systems consolidating into Meridian Health Network had no shared way to log or route a help-desk ticket, each with real trust in its own process, against a board deadline that couldn't break that trust or any one system's existing reporting. Everything that follows only makes sense once that problem is named first, the way Lesson 11 required.

The design decisions and why -- the component Lesson 11 said most candidates skip -- has three real entries written along the way. The category conflict resolved as a shared top-category model with domain-owned subcategories. The Prairie View integration chose a fifteen-minute scheduled pull over forcing a new webhook build or a manual process. The approval subflow's fail-closed design was revised to add a visible escalation path after a specific peer-review finding. Three real alternatives, three honest tradeoffs.

What was built stays brief, exactly as Lesson 11 said it should -- the catalog items, the domain-aware flow, the sync, the test plan, the documentation. The honest answer about scale matters more: this build never saw 5,000 real concurrent users or a real change-advisory board. At real scale, the sync needs load-testing against shift-change volume, the Workday and ADP integrations still need building on the proven template, and the new escalation group needs a real staffing plan.

What this hands you is a fully packaged, four-component portfolio document, written as you went rather than reconstructed from memory under interview pressure -- the exact discipline Lesson 11 asked for, now actually done. The capstone is finished and packaged. Chapter 7 picks up from here with the other half of the job search: how the interviews themselves actually run, starting with the common formats you'll walk into.
